title: Console walkthrough: usage analytics & cost breakdown - Horizon Retail
summary: Redwood AE + SE walked Horizon Retail thru Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated for a checkout chat + product recommendation workload; security and data residency flagged. Agreed next steps: share pricing and SOC2/arch docs, Lina to share benchmark script and dashboard export, schedule a 1-week pilot run to measure per-route cost and latency.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Meyers: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, and with me is Lina from our solutions engineering team. how's everyone doing?
[00:12] Tom Rivera: Good, Jordan, thanks. We had a quick sync internally about goals, so excited to see the console.
[00:22] Lina Chen: Awesome, I'll share my screen in a sec. quick agenda: usage analytics, per-route dashboards, cost breakdown and then Q&A. feel free to jump in.
[00:36] Maya Singh: Sounds good. For context, our main use case is checkout conversational assistant and a product recommendation API. both are high qps at peak.
[00:48] Carlos Perez: and infra constraints: we need to keep PCI scope minimal, prefer VPC or private deployment.
[00:57] Jordan Meyers: Totally. We'll call out Dedicated options and private deployment flows. Lina, maybe start with the usage analytics?
[01:06] Lina Chen: Sure. (screen) so this is the Console home, top panel shows token consumption by day. here's a per-route filter \u0014 you can tag routes like checkout-chat, recs-api. clicking checkout-chat shows token distribution, median latency, and cost per 1k tokens.
[01:28] Tom Rivera: When you say cost per 1k tokens, is that hosted list price or our committed dedicated rate?
[01:36] Lina Chen: by default it's hosted estimate; when you're on Dedicated we show effective unit cost based on your reserved pool. the UI overlays both so you can compare.
[01:46] Maya Singh: How accurate is the estimate for batched workloads? we batch heavily at peak.
[01:54] Lina Chen: Good question \u0014 cost model factors in batching and prefix caching. there's a toggle to simulate different batch sizes and KV cache hit rates. small note: sim is an estimate; for final numbers we recommend running a 48\u001372 hour pilot with our benchmark script.
[02:12] Carlos Perez: Is the benchmark script something we run in our infra? will it hit production models?
[02:19] Lina Chen: It's a customer-run script. it can call the hosted API or your private endpoint depending on deployment. we'll share it after the call \u0014 it'll capture tokens, latencies, qps, and route tags.
[02:30] Jordan Meyers: Also we'll include a sample dashboard export so you can drop our metrics into your observability stack.
[02:37] Tom Rivera: Cool. show me per-route latency breakdown. we care about p95 for checkout.
[02:43] Lina Chen: Right. clicking into checkout-chat shows p50/p95/p99 latencies, and a waterfall of steps \u0014 routing time, model decode, network. you can correlate spikes to model rollouts or infra events.
[02:57] Maya Singh: I see a spike here \u0014 it looks like a model fallback, can you explain?
[03:03] Lina Chen: Yeah that spike corresponds to a fallback policy: when capacity was constrained it routed to a smaller quantized variant. you can set automatic fallbacks per route or have manual controls.
[03:15] Carlos Perez: That's interesting; what about KV cache / prefix caching? we rely on session affinity.
[03:22] Lina Chen: Console shows cache hit rates by route. you can drill to see top prefixes and if you enable auto-prefetch it'll keep warm keys for active sessions. sometimes transcription will render KV cache as K-V cash or K-V 'cache' spelled weirdly \u0014 not a real issue, just the transcript.
[03:40] Tom Rivera: (laughs) noted. On security: can you show audit logs and KMS integration?
[03:46] Lina Chen: Sure. under settings -> security we have SSO (SAML), RBAC, audit logs download, and KMS/HSM key references. for Private deployments we support customer-managed KMS and VPC peering.
[03:58] Jordan Meyers: We also have SOC2 Type II report and ISO certs, happy to share.
[04:03] Maya Singh: Please, that'd help legal. also data retention \u0014 do you purge logs after 90 days by default?
[04:10] Lina Chen: Hosted default is 90 days, but you can configure retention windows. for Private you control logs retention entirely.
[04:18] Tom Rivera: Great. back to cost \u0014 can you show the per-route cost breakdown for the last 30 days?
[04:25] Lina Chen: Yep. here's a stacked view: tokens consumed and cost share by route. checkout-chat is 60% of spend, recs-api is 30%, misc is 10. we highlight hotspots \u0014 eg long context windows inflating cost.
[04:40] Maya Singh: How do you calculate cost for long context? tokens times per-token rate? do you account for kv cache to reduce repeated prefixes?
[04:47] Lina Chen: Cost = effective per-token unit * tokens consumed. the effective unit adjusts for batching and cache hits; the console will show an adjusted estimate that sometimes cuts cost by up to 40% depending on cache hit rates.
[04:59] Carlos Perez: Do you offer recommendations for quantization or model variants per route?
[05:05] Lina Chen: Yes, Optimize suggests quantization profiles and model variants based on latency/cost targets. you can run a side-by-side A/B from console and measure quality delta.
[05:15] Tom Rivera: Any examples where switching to a quantized variant harmed quality?
[05:21] Lina Chen: Rare but possible for high-precision summarization. Optimize surfaces a QA delta score from our evals; for checkout intents we see negligible quality loss often.
[05:33] Jordan Meyers: (interrupt) also worth noting we support server-side evals \u0014 you can feed in your prompt sets and we return regression alerts.
[05:41] Maya Singh: That's useful. what about routing policies? we need region-aware routing because we have EU customers.
[05:49] Lina Chen: You can set policies by latency, cost, region, or a hierarchy. we log the actual route chosen per request so Console shows a routing trace.
[05:59] Tom Rivera: Do you support fallbacks to on-prem models if cloud capacity is constrained?
[06:05] Lina Chen: For Private or Dedicated you can configure local model variants; for hosted we offer fallback to cheaper hosted variants. an example: pay-for-availability routes that can switch regions or model size automatically.
[06:18] Carlos Perez: PCI question again \u0014 will user PII or cardholder data ever hit Redwood logs on hosted?
[06:24] Jordan Meyers: Hosted can be configured to redact or never persist certain fields. for strict PCI you'd typically go Private or Dedicated to keep data in your VPC.
[06:34] Maya Singh: Ok. Can you show how tags and annotations work for teams to attribute spend?
[06:40] Lina Chen: Sure \u0014 we have per-route tags and you can attach labels like product:checkout, team:payments. then cost allocation shows by tag. you can export CSV or link to billing via API.
[06:52] Tom Rivera: And alerts for cost spikes?
[06:55] Lina Chen: Yes, threshold alerts and anomaly detection. console will notify via webhook or email.
[07:03] Jordan Meyers: Quick pause \u0014 any other security items?
[07:06] Maya Singh: Not right now, but legal will want SOC2 and architecture diagram.
[07:11] Jordan Meyers: We'll send both.
[07:13] Lina Chen: Next, quick demo of the per-request trace. (navigates) you can see request headers, model variant, tokens in/out, and the route decision. here's a sample where a request routed to dedicated pool and used prefix cache \u0014 note the reduced latencies.
[07:30] Carlos Perez: The trace shows a lot of small calls to our backend; will that increase egress?
[07:36] Lina Chen: Console shows estimated network egress; for Private deployments egress remains internal.
[07:43] Tom Rivera: Let's talk timeline: we're targeting a pilot in the next 3 weeks, 2-4 routes, want to measure cost and p95. feasible?
[07:52] Jordan Meyers: Absolutely. Lina can run the benchmark with you and we can allocate a dedicated pilot pool if needed.
[07:59] Lina Chen: I'll share the benchmark script and a runbook. typical pilot runs 48-72 hours to capture peak patterns.
[08:08] Maya Singh: We also want a sample of the per-route dashboard export so our finance team can model cost projections.
[08:15] Jordan Meyers: We'll include that in the follow-up.
[08:18] Tom Rivera: Pricing: can you give a back-of-envelope for dedicated vs hosted for our expected volume?
[08:24] Jordan Meyers: Sure \u0014 based on the numbers you gave in the pre-call (approx 10 million tokens/day peak), hosted would be roughly $X/day at list, Dedicated reserved pool could reduce your unit cost by ~30% depending on commit. I'll send a detailed pricing sheet.
[08:40] Maya Singh: We probably will get procurement involved if it's Dedicated. legal will want to see SLAs and liability clauses.
[08:47] Lina Chen: Our enterprise package includes SLA language and extended retention options. we can provision a NDA review and a SOC2 pack.
[08:56] Carlos Perez: Any known integrators or partners in Europe for Private installs? latency to eu-central matters.
[09:02] Jordan Meyers: We have partners listed in the Console docs \u0014 and we support region pinning. we'll introduce you to our partner ops contact upon request.
[09:12] Tom Rivera: Okay, last part: what do we need to provide to get the pilot started?
[09:17] Lina Chen: Keys: a list of routes to test, representative traffic pattern (token distribution), and a staging endpoint or permission to hit hosted during pilot. plus a contact for infra to coordinate quotas.
[09:30] Maya Singh: We'll provide token distribution CSV and hit patterns.
[09:34] Carlos Perez: I'll coordinate quotas and VPC peering options if Private.
[09:39] Jordan Meyers: Great. I'll recap next steps in an email.
[09:44] Tom Rivera: Nice walkthrough. quick note \u0014 we mentioned Anthropic and OpenAI earlier as comparators, curious how Redwood handles multivendor routing.
[09:55] Lina Chen: Console supports multi-model routing and you can define precedence. we also surface model quality metrics to help choose.
[10:03] Maya Singh: one more: can Optimize run periodically or is it manual?
[10:08] Lina Chen: Both \u0014 Optimize gives scheduled recommendations and you can run ad-hoc experiments.
[10:14] Jordan Meyers: Alright if there are no other questions we can wrap. Thanks everyone for the time.
[10:20] Tom Rivera: Thank you.
[10:22] Maya Singh: Thanks, very helpful.
[10:24] Carlos Perez: Thanks, talk soon.
[10:27] Jordan Meyers: We'll follow up with pricing, SOC2, benchmark script, and dashboard export.
[10:34] (call ends)
